Function Documentation

HxResult HxAlert ( uint32_t  id,
HxAlertButtonStyle_t  style,
HxImageDescription_t *  pIcon,
const char *  pTitle,
const char *  pMessage,
uint32_t *  pSelectedButton 
)

Display an alert.

HxAlert displays a standard-sized alert, and returns after the user selects a command button. The button selected by the user is returned in the pSelectedButton argument.

The style argument represents which set of command buttons should be displayed.

pIcon is a 32 by 32 image that is drawn to the left of the alert message. HxAlertGetIcon can be used to get the standard icons. If pIcon is set to NULL, no image is drawn.

pTitle is drawn in the title bar of the alert. If NULL is passed, the alert has no title.

pMessage is the body of the alert message. The string is place in a static field with no frame, to the right of the icon. If the pMessage string does not fit into the field, the system adds a frame and a scrollbar. An error is returned if this argument is NULL.

pSelectedButton in an input and output argument. For input, it signifies which command button has initial focus. For output, it communicates which command button was selected by the user. The value of 0 represents the leftmost command button ("OK" for kHxAlertStyleOKCancel or "Yes" for kHxAlertStyleYesNo). The value of 1 represents the second command button ("Cancel" for kHxAlertStyleOKCancel or "No" for kHxAlertStyleYesNo). If pSelectedButton is NULL, or if the input value of pSelectedButton is more than (number of command buttons - 1), then the initial focus is given to the leftmost command button. The output value of pSelectedButton is not defined if HxAlert does not return HX_OK.

If you pass NULL for pSelectedButton, you're telling the API that you want the first button selected and that you don't care about what button was picked. This is often used with informational alerts that only have one button.

The rightmost command button is used as the escape button (i.e., pressing the tilde key calling HxDialogCloseAllDialogs acts on this button).

Parameters:
id IN: Alert ID, or kHxWidgetAutoID to auto-generate the ID
style IN: Command button style
pIcon IN: Pointer to icon, or NULL
pTitle IN: Title of alert, or NULL
pMessage IN: String for body of alert message
pSelectedButton IN/OUT: Pointer to number of selected command button or NULL if information not needed. The value pointed to by pSelectedButton will be used to pick the button that has initial focus.
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. Returns HX_INVALID_ARG if style is not valid, or if pMessage is NULL.

HxResult HxAlertCustom ( uint32_t  id,
const HxRectangle_t *  pBounds,
HxImageDescription_t *  pIcon,
const char *  pTitle,
const char *  pMessage,
const char *  pButtonLabel1,
const char *  pButtonLabel2,
const char *  pButtonLabel3,
uint32_t *  pSelectedButton 
)

Display a custom alert.

HxAlert displays a custom alert, and returns after the user selects a command button.

If pBounds is NULL, the alert is centered in the display, and the width and height are set to kHxAlertDefaultWidth and kHxAlertDefaultHeight.

This function allows the application to customize the size of the alert window, and the command button set. At least one command button label must be defined.

pSelectedButton in an input and output argument. For input, it signifies which command button has initial focus. For output, it communicates which command button was selected by the user. The value of 0 represents the leftmost command button, 1 the second button, and 2 the third one. If pSelectedButton is NULL, or if the input value of pSelectedButton is more than (number of command buttons - 1), then the initial focus is given to the leftmost command button. The output value of pSelectedButton is not defined if HxAlertCustom does not return HX_OK.

If you pass NULL for pSelectedButton, you're telling the API that you want the first button selected and that you don't care about what button was picked. This is often used with informational alerts that only have one button.

The rightmost command button is used as the escape button (i.e., pressing the tilde key calling HxDialogCloseAllDialogs acts on this button).

Parameters:
id IN: Alert ID
pBounds IN: Bounds of the dialog, or NULL
pIcon IN: Pointer to icon, or NULL
pTitle IN: Title of alert, or NULL
pMessage IN: String for body of alert message
pButtonLabel1 IN: String for first command button
pButtonLabel2 IN: String for second command button, or NULL
pButtonLabel3 IN: String for third command button, or NULL
pSelectedButton IN/OUT: Pointer to number of selected command button or NULL if information not needed. The value pointed to by pSelectedButton will be used to pick the button that has initial focus.
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. Returns HX_INVALID_ARG if pButtonLabel1 or pMessage are NULL.

HxResult HxAlertDismiss ( uint32_t  id  ) 

Dismiss an open alert.

HxAlertDismiss causes HxAlert to return without any of the buttons having been pressed by the user. The pSelectedButton argument is set to kHxAlertNoButtonSelected.

Parameters:
selector IN: The ID of the alert to dismiss. If the ID does not match the topmost alert's id, nothing happens.
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful.

HxResult HxAlertGetIcon ( HxAlertIcon_t  selector,
HxImageDescription_t **  hIcon 
)

Accessor for standard alert icons.

HxAlertGetIcon returns one of the standard alert icons provided by the system. Normally, the application icon should be used in the application's alerts.

Parameters:
selector IN: Which icon
hIcon OUT: Returns icon image description
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful.
